f.title: Definition: serious adverse drug reaction (six criteria)
f.statement: Definition that sets the scope of the reporting duty (not a stand-alone duty): for these Regulations, a serious adverse drug reaction is any of the following resulting from the use of a drug: (1) death; (2) life-threatening; (3) permanent disability; (4) congenital malformation of a fetus or infant; (5) hospitalisation of the patient or prolongation of the patient's hospitalisation; (6) other complications that may result in permanent injury. A reaction meeting any criterion must be reported under Article 3(1); for medical care institutions and pharmacies, items 1-2 and items 3-6 carry different time limits (Article 6).
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases.

rows.actor: Medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers holding a drug manufacturing or import permit (醫療機構、藥局、藥商) (in applying the reporting duty)
rows.quote:
本辦法所稱藥品嚴重不良反應，指因使用藥品致生下列各款情形之一者：
 一、死亡。
 二、危及生命。
 三、永久性殘疾。
 四、胎兒、嬰兒先天性畸形。
 五、病人住院或延長病人住院時間。
 六、其他可能導致永久性傷害之併發症。
rows.review_note: Review: definition row kept at Mandatory (GUIDE: binding definitions that set what must be reported). Statement corrected so it does not attach the 15-day limit to all reporters; item 4 rendered from the Chinese (先天性畸形 = congenital malformation). Translation check: independent re-translation agrees. Double-check: definition, not a stand-alone duty; no modal verb in the quote, so the level rests on the GUIDE definition rule. SME review: independent re-translation of the quote agrees with quote_en in meaning, modal force, numbers and actor; level, actor, statement and tags confirmed; no change.
rows.quote_en:
For the purposes of these Regulations, a serious adverse reaction to a drug means any of the following resulting from the use of a drug:
1. Death.
2. Life-threatening.
3. Permanent disability.
4. Congenital malformation of a fetus or infant.
5. Hospitalisation of the patient or prolongation of the patient's hospitalisation.
6. Other complications that may result in permanent injury.

f.title: Report serious adverse drug reactions in the designated online system
f.statement: When medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers that hold a drug manufacturing or import permit become aware of a serious adverse drug reaction (Article 2), they shall complete a report form in the online system designated by the central competent health authority and report it to that authority.
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases. Only dealers that have obtained a drug manufacturing or import permit are "藥商" under Article 3.

f.title: Preliminary report may first be made orally, by phone, fax or e-mail
f.statement: Where necessary, the report under Article 3(1) may first be made orally or by telephone, fax or e-mail. This is a preliminary route only; the online report remains due (see the next row).

f.title: Correct an unclear or incomplete report within the time limit the authority sets
f.statement: Where the central competent health authority considers the content of a report under Article 3(1) or (2) not sufficiently clear or complete, it may order the reporter to make corrections within a set time limit; the reporter so ordered must correct the report within that time limit.

f.title: Report form may be completed in the ICH electronic transmission format
f.statement: The report form under Article 3 may be completed directly in the electronic transmission standardised format of the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH).
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases.

f.title: Include the six required items in every serious ADR report
f.statement: A report under Article 3 shall include: (1) the reporter's name and contact details, and the name and address of the reporter's place of service; (2) the date the serious adverse drug reaction occurred and the date of awareness; (3) the source of the information through which the reaction became known; (4) the patient's identification code, sex, and age or date of birth; (5) the patient's medication information; (6) the category, symptoms and related description of the reaction.
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases.

rows.quote:
第三條之通報，其內容應包括下列事項：
 一、通報人姓名、聯絡方式及其服務單位之名稱、地址。
 二、藥品嚴重不良反應發生日期及知悉日期。
 三、知悉藥品嚴重不良反應資訊來源。
 四、病人識別代號、性別，及年齡或出生日期。
 五、病人用藥資訊。
 六、藥品嚴重不良反應之類別、症狀及相關描述。
data_elements: reporter place of service name and address

rows.quote_en:
A report under Article 3 shall include the following:
1. The reporter's name and contact details, and the name and address of the reporter's place of service.
2. The date the serious adverse drug reaction occurred and the date of awareness.
3. The source of the information through which the serious adverse drug reaction became known.
4. The patient's identification code, sex, and age or date of birth.
5. The patient's medication information.
6. The category, symptoms and related description of the serious adverse drug reaction.

f.title: Institutions and pharmacies: report fatal or life-threatening serious ADRs within 7 days
f.statement: Medical care institutions and pharmacies making a report under Article 3(1) shall report a serious adverse drug reaction under Article 2 items 1 and 2 (death; life-threatening) within 7 days from the day following awareness.

Medical care institutions and pharmacies making a report under Article 3, paragraph 1, shall do so within the following time limits:

f.title: Institutions and pharmacies: report other serious ADRs within 30 days
f.statement: Medical care institutions and pharmacies making a report under Article 3(1) shall report a serious adverse drug reaction under Article 2 items 3 to 6 (permanent disability; congenital malformation; hospitalisation or prolonged hospitalisation; other complications that may cause permanent injury) within 30 days from the day following awareness.

f.title: Provide product information when an institution or pharmacy asks for it to report
f.statement: When making a report under Article 6(1), medical care institutions and pharmacies may ask the pharmaceutical dealer to provide product-related information; the pharmaceutical dealer shall not evade, obstruct or refuse.
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases.

f.title: Complete serious ADR reports within 15 days from the day after awareness
f.statement: A pharmaceutical dealer making a report under Article 3(1) shall complete it within 15 days from the day following the day it becomes aware of the matter to be reported. The day of awareness is not counted; day 1 is the next day.
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases. One time limit for all six seriousness criteria (unlike the 7/30-day split for institutions and pharmacies in Article 6).

f.title: Report new, updated or supplementary data on cases forwarded by the authority
f.statement: The central competent health authority may forward to the pharmaceutical dealer report data received from medical care institutions and pharmacies. Where, after receiving such forwarded data, the dealer has new, updated or supplementary report data, Article 3(1) and (2) and Article 7 apply mutatis mutandis: the dealer reports it in the designated online system (a preliminary oral, telephone, fax or e-mail report being allowed) within 15 days from the day following awareness.
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases. Cases first reported by medical care institutions or pharmacies and forwarded to the dealer.
f.exceptions: Only when the authority has forwarded the case and the dealer has new, updated or supplementary data.

f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Submission operations; Reconciliation

中央衛生主管機關接獲醫療機構及藥局通報藥品嚴重不良反應後，得將相關通報資料轉知藥商。
 藥商接獲中央衛生主管機關前項轉知後，有新增、更新或補充通報資料者，準用第三條第一項、第二項及前條關於通報之規定。

After receiving a report of a serious adverse drug reaction from a medical care institution or pharmacy, the central competent health authority may forward the related report data to the pharmaceutical dealer.
Where, after receiving the forwarding under the preceding paragraph from the central competent health authority, the pharmaceutical dealer has new, updated or supplementary report data, Article 3, paragraphs 1 and 2, and the provisions of the preceding article on reporting apply mutatis mutandis.

f.title: Investigate and assess causality of each serious ADR on own initiative
f.statement: When a pharmaceutical dealer becomes aware of a serious adverse drug reaction, it shall on its own initiative investigate and assess the causal relationship of the report data.
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases.

f.title: Handle unexpected or more frequent serious ADRs under Drug Safety Surveillance Article 6
f.statement: Where, based on its causality investigation and assessment, the pharmaceutical dealer finds a serious adverse drug reaction that is unexpected or occurs at a frequency higher than expected, or finds that contraindications or restrictions on use need to be added or changed, it shall act in accordance with Article 6 of the Regulations for Drug Safety Surveillance Management.

f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases.
f.exceptions: Only when the Article 9(1) assessment finds an unexpected or higher-than-expected frequency, or a need to add or change contraindications or restrictions on use.
f.processes: Signal management; Submission operations; Safety labeling

f.title: Retain serious ADR records until 5 years after the permit expires
f.statement: Pharmaceutical dealers shall retain documents and data relating to serious adverse drug reactions until five years after the validity of the drug manufacturing or import permit expires.
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases.

 一、醫療機構及藥局：至少五年。
 二、藥商：至藥品製造或輸入許可效期屆滿後五年。

rows.quote_en:
Medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers shall retain documents and data relating to serious adverse drug reactions for the following periods:
1. Medical care institutions and pharmacies: at least five years.
2. Pharmaceutical dealers: until five years after the validity of the drug manufacturing or import permit expires.

deadline_rule.clock_start: 藥品製造或輸入許可效期屆滿
deadline_rule.applies_to: Minimum retention period for serious ADR documents and data held by pharmaceutical dealers (5 years after permit expiry)

f.title: Institutions and pharmacies: retain serious ADR records for at least 5 years
f.statement: Medical care institutions and pharmacies shall retain documents and data relating to serious adverse drug reactions for at least five years.
f.clause: Article 10(1) item 1 (not curated separately in EN r1)
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases. Duty of healthcare reporters, not of the permit holder.

rows.actor: Medical care institutions and pharmacies (醫療機構及藥局)
rows.deadline: At least 5 years (start point not stated)
rows.quote:
醫療機構、藥局及藥商應保存藥品嚴重不良反應相關文件、資料；其保存期間如下：
 一、醫療機構及藥局：至少五年。
rows.location: Article 10(1) item 1 (not curated separately in EN r1)
rows.review_note: Review: new row; the EN curation mentioned this period only in brackets in the dealer row. No deadline_rule: the text gives no event that starts the five years, so no verbatim clock_start exists. Translation check: independent re-translation agrees. Double-check: quote proves actor, period and modal; start point is open, which the deadline field says. SME review: confidence 90 -> 89 for consistency with ZH-0008/0009: the actor is a healthcare reporter, not a company, so function and RACI (local-2, interfaces-3) map a hospital/pharmacy duty onto company roles by judgement.
rows.quote_en:
Medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers shall retain documents and data relating to serious adverse drug reactions for the following periods:
1. Medical care institutions and pharmacies: at least five years.

f.title: Provide retained serious ADR records on request; do not evade, obstruct or refuse
f.statement: The central competent health authority may require medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers to provide the serious ADR documents and data they retain under Article 10(1); they shall not evade, obstruct or refuse.
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases.
f.exceptions: Triggered by a request from the central competent health authority.

rows.actor: Medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers holding a drug manufacturing or import permit (醫療機構、藥局、藥商)
rows.quote: 中央衛生主管機關得要求醫療機構、藥局及藥商提供前項文件、資料；醫療機構、藥局及藥商不得規避、妨礙或拒絕。
rows.review_note: Review: actor widened to all three named in the text. Translation check: independent re-translation agrees (不得 = shall not). Double-check: quote proves actors and prohibition. SME review: independent re-translation of the quote agrees with quote_en in meaning, modal force, numbers and actor; level, actor, statement and tags confirmed; no change.
rows.quote_en: The central competent health authority may require medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers to provide the documents and data under the preceding paragraph; medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers shall not evade, obstruct or refuse.

f.title: Comply with the Personal Data Protection Act when handling ADR personal data
f.statement: When collecting, processing or using personal data under these Regulations, medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers shall act in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Act and its related laws and regulations.
f.legal_basis: Personal Data Protection Act (個人資料保護法)
f.applicability: Taiwan; Traditional Chinese original text from the Laws & Regulations Database (pcode L0030049, as amended 28 March 2024). These Regulations take effect from 1 January 2025 (Article 13). The text states no difference between domestic and foreign cases.

dates.title: Taiwan Regulations for Reporting Serious Adverse Reactions of Medicaments (amended 28 Mar 2024): take effect
dates.scope: All reporters under these Regulations: medical care institutions, pharmacies and pharmaceutical dealers holding a drug manufacturing or import permit
dates.quote: 本辦法自中華民國一百十四年一月一日施行。
dates.quote_en: These Regulations take effect on 1 January of the 114th year of the Republic of China (1 January 2025).
dates.timing_note: Republic of China year 114 = 2025 (114 + 1911). 施行 = takes effect, so kind effective. The 28 March 2024 amendment date in the page header (修正日期) is the amendment date, not an application date, and is not recorded. No transition period or separate compliance date is stated.
